title: Interleaved loadplay - bench notes and action items
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of the 'interleaved loadplay' bench we ran 2026-09-21 and working hypotheses + next steps. This is a working log — messy notes and todos.

TL;DR:
- Repro of throughput regression when mixing short (<=32) and long (>=512) sequences at realistic mix ratios.
- Baseline (homogeneous short) throughput: ~12.1k tokens/s; interleaved mix observed drop to ~7.5k tokens/s and a p99 jump from ~120ms -> ~420ms on the same fleet.
- KV-cache hit-rate fell from 88% -> 62% under loadplay because prefix sharing pattern changed; batching heuristics produced many small batches and some huge batches causing GPU scheduling jitter.
- Short-term mitigation: force smaller prefetch window + tighten batcher latency cap (owner: Priya). Longer-term: tweak batching heuristics to bias by seq-length and add per-model sequence-type routing (owner: Marco).

What we ran (bench harness):
- harness: loadplay v2 (local harness + sampler-daemon).
- config: mix_short=70%, mix_long=30% (short_len=16, long_len=1024), target_qps=340 qps, concurrency cap=48, batch_max_tokens=8192, latency_cap_ms=200
- model: rw-inference/llm-small-qa-v1 (FP16, qkv-optim kernels).
- infra: 8xA100-80GB per shard, NCCL with NVLINK enabled, same AZ.
- runs: 3x 30m steady-state windows + 3x 10m warmups.

Observations (raw):
- Aggregate throughput drop: 12.1k -> 7.5k tokens/s (steady-state), variance high across shards (stddev ~18%).
- p50 stable (~80-150ms) but p95/p99 diverge heavily after ~8 minutes into steady-state. p95 ~240ms -> 360ms, p99 peaks ~420-780ms in spikes.
- GPU util (smoothed): median 68% -> 61% on regress runs; tail GPU busy cycles show fragmentation (lots of small kernels interleaved with large matmuls).
- CPU: worker threads show increased user CPU (~+22%) and sys CPU (~+9%) — suggests more host-side scheduling/serialization overhead.
- NVLINK: counters show occasional burst saturation windows (~35% link utilization spike correlating with p99).
- KV cache: hit-rate drop from 88% (short-only) to 62% (interleaved) measured at the prefix-cache metrics emitted by the runtime.
- Batching: profiler shows many more batches <4 sequences and some batches with >32 sequences; batch size distribution bimodal.
- Memory pressure: no OOMs but pageable mem touched increased (slower CPU->GPU transfer patterns during long-kernel sequences).

Hypotheses: 
1) Batching heuristic is length-agnostic and mixes incompatible sequences, creating lots of small batches and occasional huge batches that block warp scheduling -> throughput drop and tail latency.
2) KV-cache temperature: interleaved prefix patterns reduce hot-cache locality; cache eviction increases token generation work and kernel variance.
3) NVLINK/collective stalls during large sequence matmuls (long seqs) cause stalls that amplify small-batch penalties for short seqs queued behind them.
4) Host-side scheduling: the runtime's CPU thread pool gets busier because long seqs hold the KV locks/IO longer, increasing serialization.

Quick experiments to validate (short timeline):
- E1: Force batching by sequence-length buckets (two queues: short/long) for 30m run. Compare throughput and latency. (owner: Marco, ETA: 2026-09-24).
- E2: Increase KV cache size (logical window) + prefer retention for short prefixes; measure hit-rate and throughput. (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-09-25).
- E3: Add a small artificial delay yielding time-slicing of GPU kernel launches to avoid biggest matmul preemption (simulated in harness). Check p99. (owner: Zoe, ETA: 2026-09-23).
- E4: Run same mix but with NCCL disabled (cross-check NVLINK effect) on isolated shard. (owner: Aisha, ETA: 2026-09-24).

Data snippets (from the run at 2026-09-21 14:00):
- run-id: interleave-20260921-14:00
- mean tokens/sec by shard: [7600, 8200, 7300, 7250, 7900, 7400, 7050, 7600] (avg 7500, stddev ~520)
- batch size histogram (approx): <4: 31%, 4-8: 22%, 9-16: 18%, 17-32: 12%, >32: 17%
- kv_cache_hit_rate short-only: 0.88, interleaved: 0.62
- p99 latency short-only: 0.12s, interleaved-run p99: 0.42s (spikes to 0.78s)

Notes / signal hunting tips:
- When reproducing, start with a single-shard run to eliminate cross-shard NVLINK effects. Then scale to multi-shard but keep QPS per-shard constant.
- Use flamegraphs collected by perf/py-spy and the runtime's kernel-level timestamps to correlate long matmul durations with NVLINK counters.
- Capture batch-formation logs (enable debug-batcher flag) to see exact sequences in each batch. That was very useful.
- Watch for GC/allocator hiccups on host process (tcmalloc counters spiked in one shard during the run).

Action items (clear owners + due dates):
- Priya: implement KV window tweak + run E2. Add metric emit for "kv-prefetch-misses". Due 2026-09-25.
- Marco: prototype seq-length bucketing in batcher (E1) and run single-shard smoke. Due 2026-09-24.
- Zoe: simulate kernel time-slicing in harness (E3) and share results. Due 2026-09-23.
- Aisha: NCCL-off comparison runs (E4) + NVLINK perf counters collection. Due 2026-09-24.
- Ethan (me): collect flamegraphs + combine kernel trace with NVLINK windows; create a short writeup. Due 2026-09-26.
- All: sync next on 2026-09-26 10:30 in weekly perf sync — bring run artifacts + logs.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Are we comfortable changing batching heuristics in prod without a rollout gate? Need a canary that ensures short-only workload unchanged. (product risk)
- Should we expose a per-route "seq-mix profile" so customers can opt-in to length-aware routing? That ties into routing/pinning work.
- Does Dedicated need a different default (more conservative) batching behavior?

Notes-to-self / rough followups:
- Capture one full raw GPU kernel trace (nsight) next run — currently only have timestamps + counters; need full shader timeline.
- Compare against hosted-api traces for similar mixes (ask product-hosted-api team for recent customer traces).

References:
- ENGINF-2749 (ticket with initial regression alert)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427 (batcher debug logs + feature flag)
- Slack thread: #perf-bench (linked above)

Meeting record:
- quick sync 2026-09-21 15:15 (15m): agreed experiments above. Decided to avoid changing default prod behavior until E1/E2 results.

If anything in here is unclear ping me in Slack or drop comments in the PR. This will be updated as runs complete.
